title: Conditionals and Loops
subtitle: if/elif/else, for, while, test expressions, and [[ ... ]] conditions
author: KERNAL Team

content.code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash

# [[ ]] is the modern bash conditional (prefer over [ ])
FILE="config.txt"

if [[ -f "$FILE" ]]; then
  echo "$FILE exists and is a regular file"
elif [[ -d "$FILE" ]]; then
  echo "$FILE is a directory"
else
  echo "$FILE does not exist"
fi

# Common file tests:
# -f  file exists and is a regular file
# -d  directory exists
# -e  file/directory exists
# -r  readable, -w  writable, -x  executable
# -s  file exists and is not empty

# String comparisons:
if [[ "$NAME" == "Alice" ]]; then echo "Hi Alice"; fi
if [[ "$NAME" != "" ]]; then echo "Name is set"; fi
if [[ -z "$NAME" ]]; then echo "Name is empty"; fi   # -z = zero length
if [[ -n "$NAME" ]]; then echo "Name is set"; fi     # -n = non-empty

# Number comparisons:
if [[ $AGE -gt 18 ]]; then echo "Adult"; fi
# -gt greater than, -lt less than, -ge >=, -le <=, -eq ==, -ne !=

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Loop over a list
for NAME in Alice Bob Carol; do
  echo "Hello, $NAME!"
done

# Loop over files
for FILE in *.log; do
  echo "Processing: $FILE"
  gzip "$FILE"     # compress each log file
done

# Loop over a range of numbers
for i in {1..5}; do
  echo "Iteration $i"
done

# C-style for loop
for (( i=0; i<5; i++ )); do
  echo "$i"
done

# Loop over command output
for FILE in $(find . -name '*.json'); do
  echo "Found: $FILE"
done

# Loop over script arguments
for ARG in "$@"; do
  echo "Arg: $ARG"
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# while: loop while condition is true
COUNT=0
while [[ $COUNT -lt 5 ]]; do
  echo "Count: $COUNT"
  (( COUNT++ ))   # increment
done

# Read file line by line
while IFS= read -r LINE; do
  echo "Line: $LINE"
done < input.txt

# Wait for a service to be ready
until curl -s http://localhost:3000/health; do
  echo "Waiting for server..."
  sleep 2
done
echo "Server is ready!"

# Infinite loop with break
while true; do
  if [[ -f /tmp/stop ]]; then
    break
  fi
  echo "Running..."
  sleep 10
done

questions.question: You want to check if a variable $ENVIRONMENT equals 'production'. Which is correct bash syntax?
questions.explanation: In bash, [[ ... ]] is the modern conditional test. Use == for string comparison inside [[ ]]. The spaces before and after == are required. The semicolon before then is required (or put then on the next line). Single = is assignment in shell, not comparison (though it also works in old [ ] style tests for historical reasons).

faq.q: What is the difference between [ ] and [[ ]]?
faq.a: [ ] is the POSIX test command — works in all shells but has edge cases with spaces in variable names (use quotes: [ "$VAR" ]). [[ ]] is a bash/zsh keyword — safer (no word splitting), supports &&/||/=~, and doesn't require quoting variables for most comparisons. Always use [[ ]] in bash scripts.

examples: for ENV in staging production; do ssh $ENV 'sudo systemctl restart app'; done — restart across multiple environments
while ! pg_isready; do sleep 1; done — wait for PostgreSQL to be ready in Docker Compose startup scripts
